column1: # Mega Man Battle Network Legacy Collection Vol. 1 on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# A GBA emulator collection (Battle Network 1, 2, 3 White and 3 Blue) with a NoesisGUI launcher, SDK 13.3.5, NVN, Wwise; subsdk1 is NintendoSDK_movie. Update v131072 (1.0.2).
# Tested 2026-11-12 on an AYN Odin 2 (QCS8550, Adreno 740, Android 13) with Mesa Turnip (--vulkan-driver), driven with DM_CTL: the intro movies, the title, the main menu,
# Battle Network 1 started from it, its title and opening (dialogue, walking Lan's room), the in-game options overlay, Return to the Title Screen and Quit back to the main menu.
# 60 fps without a cap to remove: the collection presents every frame (interval 1); BN1's opening p99 16.67 ms, 0 dropped frames in 300, footprint 1.35 GB, no audio underrun.
# What it needed from the core: the replay fenced NVNsync objects the game had already freed at the end of each intro movie (sync_replay_fence, nvn_obj.h), which corrupted the
# heap's free list and crashed the next allocation (TlsHeapCache, from movie::NnExtractor::GetTrackFormat) about 15 s in, the crash an experimental port hit before this profile;
# and nvnDeviceGetWindowOriginMode, whose unimplemented 0 (lower left) drew a mirrored copy of the launcher's menu over the top of the screen.
# 2026-11-14, played on the Odin 2 by a player: Battle Network 1, 2 and 3 saved, loaded, fought, explored their maps, and the gallery opened, all without a fault.
# The adaptive frame rate is off (DM_ADAPTIVE_FPS=0): the game paces itself to the vsync inside its own frame, so the work the rate judges sat at the period (p50 16.6 / p90 16.7 ms
# at 60 fps). Any hiccup stepped it down (8 busy CPU loops for 20 s at the title: 60 -> 40 -> 30 fps, 246 then 150 of 300 frames dropped), and at the longer period the same
# self-pacing kept the work over 16.7 ms (p90 21 ms), so it never climbed back until a restart; the 40 fps step also shows as 30 on a 60 Hz screen. As the collection runs its GBA
# games one frame per present, every step down slowed the game too (players saw 40, then 30 fps at half speed, at boot or in battles). With the rate held at the game's own
# interval the same load dropped 0-2 of 300 frames, at the title and in BN1's first room, and it stays at 60 fps with or without --fps60 (FPSLocker-Warehouse has no config for
# this build and none is needed).
# CPU (2026-11-14, top -H): in BN1's first room the process takes about 58 % of one core: the game's main thread 19 %, and the movie decoder 20 % plus MediaCodec's threads 4 %.
# The launcher keeps its 1080p H.264 background video playing behind the GBA screen and fetches every frame (GetOutputBuffer 80 of 80 in a trace), which the Switch's
# decoder and GPU do for free and the host decodes and converts to RGBA on the CPU. Turning ADPF off (DM_NO_ADPF=1) changed no clock: the Odin 2 holds its clocks up even on
# its home screen. A cheaper movie path is a core change for every movie game, not this profile's.
# Known gaps: the launcher builds shaders in memory that are in no game file (whole GLSLC outputs in the heap, not from glslcCompile or any RomFS file; the same 13 in Vol. 2).
# A shader is captured on the device the first time a draw needs it, and only a port with --install pulls the captures into the game folder's build folder, which keeps them:
# a port into a new folder (or after its build folder was deleted) shows black menu backgrounds until a run and one more port with --install. Neither the device nor Turnip is
# the cause. Qualcomm's own driver on the Odin 2 (512.676, Vulkan 1.3.128) crashes in vkCmdBeginRenderPass on the first pass after the intro movie; with DM_VK_RP=0 (dynamic
# rendering) it runs, at 30 fps (frame work p50 24 ms): port with Turnip.
